observations.finding: vs DMSO f_a8be9aee1b01 (dense monolayer of small compact mononucleate cells, uniform blue nuclei, ~100+ cells/field) treated fields are sparser with large black background: f_6432e356ed2e ~90% empty (only ~8 cells at top edge) and f_a02f9f4e3a42 ~50% empty right half; f_677b431624c9 and f_dfd5aef231d8 show moderate gaps and dispersed clusters (Blue DNA, green tubulin, red actin, same contrast)

Cell footprint markedly enlarged and spread: extensive green tubulin + red cortical actin cytoplasm around blue nuclei; flat giant cells e.g. f_677b431624c9 right-center, f_dfd5aef231d8 center-right, f_a02f9f4e3a42 bottom-center. Quantitative increase in cytoplasmic area with larger major axis.
Blue DNA nuclei enlarged in treated vs DMSO uniform small ovals; some very large pale blue nuclei and nuclear pleomorphism visible in all treated fields

Multinucleation/polyploid giant cells: single continuous green/red cytoplasm containing 2-4 distinct blue nuclei e.g. f_677b431624c9 bottom cluster 6-8 cells, f_dfd5aef231d8 center and bottom clusters, f_a02f9f4e3a42 top cluster with 4 nuclei and long tubulin bridge. No direct bi-nucleate count in provided features; proxy is frac_large_nucleus but not same.

Cell shape more irregular and less compact: ruffled red F-actin periphery, protrusive, lower roundness/solidity vs DMSO ovals. Matches reduced roundness/solidity/eccentricity and increased cell_nuc_area_ratio (cytoplasm expanded more than nucleus)

F-actin (red) remains cortical at periphery and beta-tubulin (green) remains diffuse filamentous throughout enlarged cytoplasm; no loss, collapse, puncta or dense bundles to suggest actin disruption or microtubule depolymerization/stabilization

Sparse bright condensed mitotic-like figures (yellow-white co-localization of DNA/tubulin/actin) e.g. f_677b431624c9 center, f_dfd5aef231d8 top-left and bottom-left, f_a02f9f4e3a42 bottom. Increased vs DMSO 1-2% mitoses

notable_cells.why: paradigm giant flat cell: huge green/red cytoplasm, single enlarged blue nucleus, exemplifies cell_area 7191 vs 3839 DMSO (z 23.49) and nuc_area 1080 vs 749 (z 7.04)
paradigm polyploid cluster: large flat cell with 2 pale nuclei + irregular neighbours, shows cell_area z 9.8 and frac_large_nucleus z 17.5
bi-nucleate giant with long green tubulin connection, demonstrates failed cytokinesis / reduced roundness z -5.3 and solidity no
sparse field example: only 5-6 enlarged cells present, consistent with cytostatic/toxic low density but not in top deviations

candidate_mechanisms.why: Best match: markedly increased cell_area/cell_major_axis (z 10-23), nuc_area/nuc_major_axis, frac_large_nucleus (z 5-17), cell_nuc_area_ratio, reduced roundness/solidity, multinucleate polyploid giant cells with intact actin/tubulin and modest mitotic increase. Failed cytokinesis without microtubule disruption is classic Aurora. z-scores consistent across 1,3,10 uM wells w_1777b23edf(w_1777), w_651d1c1603, w_13e020007c.
Alternative DNA damage/replication also enlarges nuclei but does not typically produce the prominent multinucleate flat giant cells; no cytoskeletal collapse to support Microtubule/Actin MoA.

report.uncertainty: Moderate: phenotype strongly polyploid/Aurora-like, but without phospho-histone or ploidy quantification cannot exclude general DNA damage induced G2 arrest; microtubule/actin disruptor excluded by preserved red cortical actin and green diffuse tubulin.

data.note:
Correct call: DNA replication. Floxuridine (FUDR, CID 5790) is a thymidylate synthase inhibitor (ChEMBL CHEMBL917, target CHEMBL1952) – name/structure agree – causing dTTP depletion, replication fork collapse and S-phase stress, annotated in BBBC021 as DNA replication.

Evidence: NSC 3/4 DNA replication (mitoxantrone similarity 0.895, 0.807) vs split kNN 5/10 Aurora (AZ-A), with non-monotonic mitotic spike (frac_mitotic_like rho -0.11 p0.89, single-well z 10.37 at 1 µM) and large-nucleus rho 0.4 p0.6, enlarged cell_area/nuc_area but preserved cortical actin/diffuse tubulin excluding actin/microtubule MoAs. Literature supports 5-fluorodeoxyuridine blocking replication via UNG-escape and fork collapse PMID 27517750, 26494862.

Uncertainty remains due to 0/4 budget preventing requested dose-index-3 rep2 validation; Aurora-like polyploid giant-cell visual was noted but contradicted by DNA-content and cytoskeletal trends.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound: floxuridine (PubChem CID 5790, ChEMBL CHEMBL917) - Thymidylate synthase inhibitor, name and BBBC021 structure agree (e27,e28). Verdict correct: we submitted DNA replication (p=0.55 then p=0.52) and truth = DNA replication. Ground truth mechanism maps to DNA replication class: thymidylate synthase inhibition depletes dTTP / incorporates 5-FdU and blocks DNA replication. This is consistent with PMID 27517750 which reports 5-fluorodeoxyuridine induces replication fork collapse, and PMID 26494862 which reports incorporated 5-FU blocks DNA replication. The megaloblastic / enlarged nucleus phenotype we observed is the expected cellular consequence, PMID 6450011 describes drug-induced megaloblastic change.

What got it right:
- Core morphological signal was large-nucleus / large-cell with increased DNA content. Wells w_1777b23edf (1 uM) cell_area z=+23.5, frac_large_nucleus z=+14.6, cell_major_axis z=+11.9 (e3) and w_651d1c1603 (3 uM) frac_large_nucleus z=+17.5, cell_area z=+9.8 (e4) and w_13e020007c (10 uM) cell_area z=+11.0, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+7.6 (e2) were extreme, consistent with S-phase arrest and nuclear enlargement rather than mitotic rounding. Dose_response of nuc_dna_integrated Spearman rho=+1.00 p=0 (e12,e22) replicated twice was the strongest monotonic signal, supporting progressive DNA accumulation without division - key for replication stress vs. mitotic arrest.
- Reference atlas NSC vote 3/4 DNA replication (e7,e17) was correct and we weighted it over k-neighbour vote. The split was informative but we correctly prioritized NSC: kNN 5/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors, 3/10 DNA replication, 2/10 DNA damage (e7,e17) shows phenotypic overlap between replication-induced large nuclei/polyploidy and Aurora polyploidy.
- Exclusion logic was correct: frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.11 p=0.89 (e10,e18) showed no monotonic mitotic accumulation, which contradicts sustained Aurora kinase inhibition which predicts elevated p-H3 mitotic fraction and >4N multinucleates. Tubulin and actin metrics rho=-0.20 to -0.40 p=0.6-0.8 (e13,e19,e20) correctly excluded microtubule/actin MoAs we tested.

What misled / created uncertainty:
- describe_phenotype (e6): microscopist noted density lower vs DMSO, listed Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates on 4 fields. Visually enlarged/flattened cells with low density can resemble Aurora polyploidy to a human scorer, especially at single field without DNA quantitation.
- That visual prior plus kNN Aurora majority 5/10 made Aurora a persistent alternative in hypotheses history: 0.30 then 0.33 (e15,e25). Review correctly flagged this split: atlas kNN majority Aurora vs NSC minority, and single-well mitosis spike non-monotonic. We kept DNA replication on top but probability dropped from 0.60 to 0.52 reflecting this conflict.
- Low-dose well w_62dd17d7bc (0.3 uM, 24 cells measured) gave cell_roundness z=+9.5, cell_area z=+5.8, frac_multinucleate_proxy z=-4.5 (e5). Low n=24 made this a noisy outlier. At higher doses frac_large_nucleus and cell_area peaked at 1-3 uM (z=+23.5/+17.5) then declined at 10 uM (z=+11.0), producing non-monotonic dose_response rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for both (e8,e9,e24) and nuc_area rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e11). With only 4 wells/doses tested, p-values were unpowered and we could not distinguish true biphasic toxicity from sampling noise.
- frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e21) trended up, which could superficially support Aurora, but p non-significant and early point was strongly negative, so we correctly did not overweight it. cell_count rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e14,e23) showed no clear viability loss, also surprising for a cytotoxic antimetabolite, but again underpowered n=4 and limited dose coverage.

Acquisition choice - why uncertainty remained:
- We started with 8 doses available and 4/4 well budget (e1). We acquired only rep1 at 10 uM, 1 uM, 3 uM, 0.3 uM (e2-e5) - a sensible range-finding set covering onset to mid-high dose to avoid extreme toxicity, but we exhausted budget. We never sampled 30-100 uM or any replicate 2.
- Requested experiment was re-run atlas + mitotic-fraction on dose index 3 replicate 2 before accepting DNA replication. We re-ran compare_to_reference_atlas and multiple dose_responses (e17-e24) but had 0/4 budget left, so could not acquire w_??? rep2. This left contradictions unexplained and probability uncalibrated, as flagged: DNA replication under-supported given non-monotonic large-nucleus trend and reliance on perfect nuc_dna_integrated rho=+1.00 based on only 4 points.
- Literature search PubMed 'floxuridine thymidylate synthase inhibitor DNA replication' returned 15 hits/5 returned (e29) and replication-stress enlarged nuclei query 0 hits (e30) - we had not incorporated those hits into the blinded call, but post-unblinding they support the mechanism without changing the dose-response limitations.

Lesson: For antimetabolites where cell/nuclear enlargement mimics Aurora polyploidy morphologically, integrated DNA intensity dose trend and lack of monotonic mitotic-like increase are more discriminative than single-well z-scores or kNN plurality. Future runs need budget for at least one replicate at the phenotypic peak (1-3 uM here) and a high-dose well plus orthogonal S-phase vs M-phase marker as we proposed (p-H3 Ser10 / gammaH2AX / EdU + DNA flow), but those data were not acquired in this run. This reflection is for screening assay interpretation only and is not clinical advice.

e12,e22 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+1.00 supported S-phase DNA accumulation
e7,e17 NSC 3/4 DNA replication correctly prioritized over kNN Aurora 5/10 overlap
e10,e18 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.11 excluded sustained Aurora mitotic arrest; e13,e19,e20 flat tub/actin excluded cytoskeletal MoA
what_was_wrong: e6 microscopist Aurora candidate and e17 kNN 5/10 Aurora inflated Aurora posterior 0.30-0.33
e5 low-n well and e8,e9,e24 non-monotonic rho=+0.40 p=0.6 left large-nucleus trend underpowered
budget 4/4 spent prevented requested rep2 high-dose validation, leaving probability 0.52 uncalibrated

For assay validation only: acquire replicate 2 at 1 and 3 uM + 30 uM well with p-H3 Ser10 / gammaH2AX / EdU and DNA flow to distinguish S-phase arrest (gammaH2AX pan-nuclear, EdU reduced, no persistent p-H3) from Aurora polyploidy (persistent p-H3, >4N). Already suggested in e16/e26 and would have addressed split vote.

## Reflection

Unblinded compound: floxuridine (PubChem CID 5790, ChEMBL CHEMBL917) - Thymidylate synthase inhibitor, name and BBBC021 structure agree (e27,e28). Verdict correct: we submitted DNA replication (p=0.55 then p=0.52) and truth = DNA replication. Ground truth mechanism maps to DNA replication class: thymidylate synthase inhibition depletes dTTP / incorporates 5-FdU and blocks DNA replication. This is consistent with PMID 27517750 which reports 5-fluorodeoxyuridine induces replication fork collapse, and PMID 26494862 which reports incorporated 5-FU blocks DNA replication. The megaloblastic / enlarged nucleus phenotype we observed is the expected cellular consequence, PMID 6450011 describes drug-induced megaloblastic change.

What got it right:
- Core morphological signal was large-nucleus / large-cell with increased DNA content. Wells w_1777b23edf (1 uM) cell_area z=+23.5, frac_large_nucleus z=+14.6, cell_major_axis z=+11.9 (e3) and w_651d1c1603 (3 uM) frac_large_nucleus z=+17.5, cell_area z=+9.8 (e4) and w_13e020007c (10 uM) cell_area z=+11.0, cell_nuc_area_ratio z=+7.6 (e2) were extreme, consistent with S-phase arrest and nuclear enlargement rather than mitotic rounding. Dose_response of nuc_dna_integrated Spearman rho=+1.00 p=0 (e12,e22) replicated twice was the strongest monotonic signal, supporting progressive DNA accumulation without division - key for replication stress vs. mitotic arrest.
- Reference atlas NSC vote 3/4 DNA replication (e7,e17) was correct and we weighted it over k-neighbour vote. The split was informative but we correctly prioritized NSC: kNN 5/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors, 3/10 DNA replication, 2/10 DNA damage (e7,e17) shows phenotypic overlap between replication-induced large nuclei/polyploidy and Aurora polyploidy.
- Exclusion logic was correct: frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.11 p=0.89 (e10,e18) showed no monotonic mitotic accumulation, which contradicts sustained Aurora kinase inhibition which predicts elevated p-H3 mitotic fraction and >4N multinucleates. Tubulin and actin metrics rho=-0.20 to -0.40 p=0.6-0.8 (e13,e19,e20) correctly excluded microtubule/actin MoAs we tested.

What misled / created uncertainty:
- describe_phenotype (e6): microscopist noted density lower vs DMSO, listed Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates on 4 fields. Visually enlarged/flattened cells with low density can resemble Aurora polyploidy to a human scorer, especially at single field without DNA quantitation.
- That visual prior plus kNN Aurora majority 5/10 made Aurora a persistent alternative in hypotheses history: 0.30 then 0.33 (e15,e25). Review correctly flagged this split: atlas kNN majority Aurora vs NSC minority, and single-well mitosis spike non-monotonic. We kept DNA replication on top but probability dropped from 0.60 to 0.52 reflecting this conflict.
- Low-dose well w_62dd17d7bc (0.3 uM, 24 cells measured) gave cell_roundness z=+9.5, cell_area z=+5.8, frac_multinucleate_proxy z=-4.5 (e5). Low n=24 made this a noisy outlier. At higher doses frac_large_nucleus and cell_area peaked at 1-3 uM (z=+23.5/+17.5) then declined at 10 uM (z=+11.0), producing non-monotonic dose_response rho=+0.40 p=0.6 for both (e8,e9,e24) and nuc_area rho=+0.20 p=0.8 (e11). With only 4 wells/doses tested, p-values were unpowered and we could not distinguish true biphasic toxicity from sampling noise.
- frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e21) trended up, which could superficially support Aurora, but p non-significant and early point was strongly negative, so we correctly did not overweight it. cell_count rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e14,e23) showed no clear viability loss, also surprising for a cytotoxic antimetabolite, but again underpowered n=4 and limited dose coverage.

Acquisition choice - why uncertainty remained:
- We started with 8 doses available and 4/4 well budget (e1). We acquired only rep1 at 10 uM, 1 uM, 3 uM, 0.3 uM (e2-e5) - a sensible range-finding set covering onset to mid-high dose to avoid extreme toxicity, but we exhausted budget. We never sampled 30-100 uM or any replicate 2.
- Requested experiment was re-run atlas + mitotic-fraction on dose index 3 replicate 2 before accepting DNA replication. We re-ran compare_to_reference_atlas and multiple dose_responses (e17-e24) but had 0/4 budget left, so could not acquire w_??? rep2. This left contradictions unexplained and probability uncalibrated, as flagged: DNA replication under-supported given non-monotonic large-nucleus trend and reliance on perfect nuc_dna_integrated rho=+1.00 based on only 4 points.
- Literature search PubMed 'floxuridine thymidylate synthase inhibitor DNA replication' returned 15 hits/5 returned (e29) and replication-stress enlarged nuclei query 0 hits (e30) - we had not incorporated those hits into the blinded call, but post-unblinding they support the mechanism without changing the dose-response limitations.

Lesson: For antimetabolites where cell/nuclear enlargement mimics Aurora polyploidy morphologically, integrated DNA intensity dose trend and lack of monotonic mitotic-like increase are more discriminative than single-well z-scores or kNN plurality. Future runs need budget for at least one replicate at the phenotypic peak (1-3 uM here) and a high-dose well plus orthogonal S-phase vs M-phase marker as we proposed (p-H3 Ser10 / gammaH2AX / EdU + DNA flow), but those data were not acquired in this run. This reflection is for screening assay interpretation only and is not clinical advice.

What was right:
- e3,e4,e2 extreme frac_large_nucleus and cell_area z-scores signaled replication stress enlarged nuclei
- e12,e22 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+1.00 supported S-phase DNA accumulation
- e7,e17 NSC 3/4 DNA replication correctly prioritized over kNN Aurora 5/10 overlap
- e10,e18 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.11 excluded sustained Aurora mitotic arrest; e13,e19,e20 flat tub/actin excluded cytoskeletal MoA

What was wrong or missed:
- e6 microscopist Aurora candidate and e17 kNN 5/10 Aurora inflated Aurora posterior 0.30-0.33
- e5 low-n well and e8,e9,e24 non-monotonic rho=+0.40 p=0.6 left large-nucleus trend underpowered
- budget 4/4 spent prevented requested rep2 high-dose validation, leaving probability 0.52 uncalibrated

Proposed next experiment: Not a clinical recommendation. For assay validation only: acquire replicate 2 at 1 and 3 uM + 30 uM well with p-H3 Ser10 / gammaH2AX / EdU and DNA flow to distinguish S-phase arrest (gammaH2AX pan-nuclear, EdU reduced, no persistent p-H3) from Aurora polyploidy (persistent p-H3, >4N). Already suggested in e16/e26 and would have addressed split vote.
